Dear Secretary Reese:

       On July 24, 2026, Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (MISO),1 on behalf
of American Transmission Company LLC (ATC), submitted four amended and executed Large
Load Project Commitment Agreements (LLPCAs)2 and an executed Minimum Transmission
Charge Agreement (MTCA)3 between ATC and Wisconsin Electric Power Company (WEPCo).

       On September 22, 2026, Commission staff issued a deficiency letter in the above docket
requesting additional information to process the filing (Deficiency Letter). This submittal
responds to the Deficiency Letter (Deficiency Response).

I.      RESPONSE TO DEFICIENCY LETTER

     1. The introductory paragraph of each LLPCA states, in part, that the LLPCA is
        “effective upon receipt of all required regulatory approvals contemplated by
        Section 3.9 hereof.” Section 3.9 (Disputes) of each LLPCA does not address
        regulatory approvals.

            a. Please explain the discrepancy in the reference to section 3.9.

            b. Please explain whether there are any pending regulatory approvals, or if
               any regulatory approval was granted after July 1, 2026. If so, please
               explain how this reconciles with ATC’s requested July 1, 2026 effective date
               in the instant filing and whether this would impact the collection of the
               CWIP Charge.

ATC Response:

        The reference to Section 3.9 in the introductory paragraph was an error. The correct
section reference should be Section 3.11, which provides the required regulatory approvals for
the LLPCAs. With this Deficiency Response, ATC is submitting substitute amended LLPCAs
to replace the amended LLPCAs filed on July 24, 2026 in this docket. The substitute amended
LLPCAs correct this section reference, along with other changes as noted in this Deficiency
Response. A redline version of the substitute amended LLPCAs is also provided.

        ATC and WEPCo submitted the amended LLPCAs to the Public Service Commission of
Wisconsin (PSCW) in Dockets 5-AE-246 and 5-AE-284, respectively, for approval as affiliated
interest agreements in accordance with Wis. Stat § 196.52. As of the date of this Deficiency
Response, those dockets remain under review at the PSCW. No other regulatory approvals are
required.

        ATC intends to begin collection of the CWIP charge from WEPCo as soon as the
required regulatory approvals are obtained, with a catch-up billing going back to the requested
effective date of July 1, 2026, if that date is approved by the Commission.


     2. Section 3.3 (Obligation to Reimburse Project Costs) of each LLPCA states that
        upon termination, cancellation, or substantial change, WEPCo shall reimburse to
        ATC all expenditures, costs, and cancellation fees incurred, or due to commitments
        made by ATC (collectively, Project Costs) to construct the facilities described in
        Exhibit A to each LLPCA (LLPCA Project). In addition, section 3.3 of each
        LLPCA describes the obligation of WEPCo to reimburse ATC for Project Costs,
        stating in part, “[i]n the event of termination of this [LLPCA] due to the
        completion of the [LLPCA Project], and the [LLPCA Project] being put into ATC’s
        rate base (as described in Section 3.10(a)), the reimbursement obligation set forth
 October 22, 2026
Page 3


       in this Section 3.3 shall not apply.” The LLPCAs do not contain section 3.10(a).

              Please indicate the applicable section in the LLPCA that describes the
              LLPCA Project being put into ATC’s rate base such that the
              reimbursement obligation set forth in section 3.3 shall not apply.

ATC Response:

       The reference to Section 3.10(a) in Section 3.3 was an error. The correct section
reference should be Section 3.12(a). The substitute amended LLPCAs submitted with this
Deficiency Response correct this section reference.


   3. Section 5.1 (Survival) of each LLPCA states that, “[WEPCo]’s obligations under
      Sections 3.3, 3.4 and 3.6 shall survive any termination or cancellation of this
      Agreement.” The amended LLPCAs include a new section 3.5 (Amounts to Be
      Directly Charged), and as a result, sections 3.6 (Mitigation) and 3.7 (Payment of
      Reimbursable Project Costs) have been renumbered.

              Please confirm whether section 5.1 of each LLPCA intends to refer to
              section 3.6 or if it should be revised to refer to section 3.7.

ATC Response:

       Section 5.1 (Survival) of each amended LLPCA has been revised in the substitute
amended LLPCAs to reference Sections 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8. Each of those sections is
intended to survive any termination or cancellation of the Agreement.

   4. Section 3.4 (Amounts to be Reimbursed) of each LLPCA states that upon
      termination, cancellation, or substantial change of the LLPCA, WEPCo will
      reimburse ATC for the Project Costs, including any applicable tax gross-up
      charges. In the event the LLPCA Project is terminated, cancelled, or substantially
      changed:

           a. Please provide ATC’s proposed accounting for its receipt of WEPCo’s
              reimbursement for the incurred Project Costs, including the gross-up for
              the current tax liability that ATC would be responsible to remit to the
              Internal Revenue Service. In addition, please confirm that ATC will
              separately record the portion of the cash receipt related to the tax gross-up
              from the portion related to the cancelled LLPCA Project.

           b. Please explain how the tax gross-up charges are calculated. In addition,
              please clarify whether the tax gross-up charges will be determined based on
              the tax rates reflected in ATC’s formula rate in Attachment O of MISO’s
 October 22, 2026
Page 4


             Tariff.

ATC Response:

      a. Under the LLPCA, the tax gross-up is only applicable if the project is terminated,
         cancelled, or substantially changed and ATC still has a capital asset, for income tax
         purposes, created during construction that is able to be placed in-service as used and
         useful. In that case, ATC would bill WEPCo for the capital cost of the asset plus the
         tax gross-up. The amount reimbursed for the capital cost will be credited to the
         assets in FERC Account 101 and reduce ATC’s rate base as a taxable Contribution in
         Aid of Construction (CIAC). The accumulated deferred income tax (ADIT) created
         from this taxable reimbursement in the form of a deferred tax asset will be excluded
         from ATC’s rate base and, therefore, the ADIT will not be included in ATC’s rates.
         The tax gross-up portion of the reimbursement will be separately recorded to below-
         the-line revenue account 421. Recording the tax gross-up to a below-the-line
         revenue account makes ATC’s owners whole for the tax consequences of the
         reimbursement and does not impact customer rates. As a limited liability company,
         ATC is taxed as a partnership and it does not remit taxes directly to the IRS. That is
         the responsibility of ATC’s taxable owners that are taxed as corporations. The tax
         gross-up addresses the current tax liability of the owners and ATC collects it on their
         behalf. There is no tax gross-up calculated on our tax-exempt ownership.

      b. The tax gross-up is calculated to address the tax timing difference created by the
         taxable CIAC, which results from the reimbursement of the capital asset costs.
         Upon ATC’s reimbursement in the form of a taxable CIAC, ATC will credit taxable
         income and create a tax basis only asset for the portion of the reimbursement that is
         not the tax gross-up. This new tax basis-only asset will be classified as an electric
         transmission class asset subject to a 15-year Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery
         System (“MACRS”) depreciation life in accordance with IRS rules. The taxes paid
         on the immediate recognition of income upon reimbursement will be subsequently
         recovered as a tax timing difference over the 15-year tax life of the tax basis-only
         asset. The tax gross-up represents the present value of this timing difference
         between when the taxes are initially paid upon reimbursement versus the
         recognition of the depreciation deductions over the 15-year tax life of the asset. The
         tax rate used in the calculation of the tax gross-up is the 21% federal tax rate plus
         the weighted state effective tax rates from Attachment O adjusted down to exclude
         ATC’s tax-exempt ownership. Additionally, the discount rate used in the present
         value calculation is representative of ATC’s weighted average cost of capital from
         Attachment O, grossed up for taxes. An illustrative example is shown below:

   5. Section 9(B)(c)(i)(2) of the MTCA states, “If during the term of the MTCA the
      aggregate, cumulative amount of Minimum Transmission Charge and the
      Customer Load Project Schedule 9 Charge paid by [WEPCo] reaches the
      Minimum Transmission Charge Liability Cap, [WEPCo] will no longer pay the
      Minimum Transmission Charge” (emphasis added).

            a. Please confirm whether WEPCo will pay the customer load project
               Schedule 9 charge under this MTCA and, if so, please explain whether this
               charge is duplicative of the monthly payments WEPCo makes under
               Schedule 9-ATC of MISO’s Tariff given that section 9(B) of the MTCA
 October 22, 2026
Page 6


              states, “For clarity, separate from this MTCA, [WEPCo] remains
              responsible for paying the Network Integration Transmission Service
              Charge pursuant to Schedule 9-ATC of the MISO Tariff.”

                   i. If WEPCo will not pay the customer load project Schedule 9
                      charge under this MTCA, please confirm whether the minimum
                      transmission charge liability cap applies to the aggregate,
                      cumulative amount of minimum transmission charges paid by
                      WEPCo under the MTCA and the amount ATC recovers from
                      WEPCo for the T-D Project under Schedule 9-ATC of MISO’s
                      Tariff.

ATC Response:

ATC confirms that WEPCo will not pay a separate Schedule 9 charge under the MTCA.
WEPCo will pay Schedule 9 charges under the MISO Tariff for its total load, including the
Microsoft load referenced in the MTCA (see Sections 9(B) and 6(A)). The MTCA thus does
not impose a charge that is duplicative of the monthly payments WEPCo pays under Schedule
9-ATC. WEPCo will report the Microsoft load as a separate part of its Load Ratio Share under
Schedule 9-ATC to enable measurement of that load for purposes of calculating the Minimum
Transmission Charge under the MTCA.

The MTCA requires that WEPCo pay a Minimum Transmission Charge, calculated as the
difference between WEPCo’s Requested Transmission Capacity for the Microsoft load and the
actual monthly load served under Schedule 9-ATC of the Tariff times the Schedule 9-ATC rate.
If the actual monthly load served under Schedule 9-ATC is less than the Requested
Transmission Capacity, WEPCo will be charged a Minimum Transmission Charge for the
difference at the Schedule 9-ATC rate such that WEPCo pays the Schedule 9-ATC rate for the
full amount of the Requested Transmission Capacity.

The amount WEPCo pays as a Minimum Transmission Charge (i.e., the difference between the
actual load and the Requested Transmission Capacity) is subject to a cap, based on the
aggregate of charges paid by WEPCo under the MTCA and Schedule 9-ATC.

Once WEPCo’s payments – calculated as the sum of the Schedule 9-ATC charges plus the
Minimum Transmission Charges – have reached the amount shown in Exhibit F of the MTCA ,
WEPCO will no longer be subject to a Minimum Transmission Charge and will continue to pay
only Schedule 9-ATC (i.e., actual load) charges (see Section Sec. 9.B.c.i.2).


   6. Section 9(B)(c)(i)(3) of the MTCA states, “The Minimum Transmission Charge
      Liability Cap applies to any Early Termination Fee incurred pursuant to this
      MTCA.” Section 14(F)(b) (Early Termination Fee) states, “The Early Termination
      Fee will equal the aggregate monthly Requested Transmission Capacity multiplied
 October 22, 2026
Page 7


       by the Network Rate in effect at the time of the termination event for the
       remainder of the Term of this MTCA.”

           a. Please confirm, if WEPCo pays ATC an early termination fee,
              whether the minimum transmission charge liability cap applies to the
              aggregate, cumulative amount of minimum transmission charges, the
              customer load project Schedule 9 charge, and the early termination
              fee.

                   i. Alternatively, if WEPCo does not pay the customer load project
                      Schedule 9 charge under this MTCA, please confirm, if WEPCo
                      pays ATC an early termination fee, whether the minimum
                      transmission charge liability cap applies to the aggregate, cumulative
                      amount of minimum transmission charges, the amount ATC
                      recovers from WEPCo for the T-D Project under Schedule 9-ATC of
                      MISO’s Tariff, and the early termination fee.

ATC Response:

ATC can confirm that as stated in the filed MTCA, Commission Staff has correctly interpreted
the Minimum Transmission Charge Liability Cap as applying to the aggregate, cumulative
amount of Minimum Transmission Charges, plus the Schedule 9-ATC load charges. The
Minimum Transmission Charge Liability Cap also was intended to apply to the Early
Termination Fee – i.e., the aggregate monthly Requested Transmission Capacity multiplied by
the Network Rate in effect at the time of termination for the remainder of the agreement’s term.

However, after further consideration, ATC and WEPCo have agreed that the Early Termination
Fee should be revised to equal the remaining net book value of the Transmission Project at the
time of termination. With this Deficiency Response, ATC is submitting a substitute MTCA to
replace the MTCA filed on July 24, 2026 in this docket.

Also, because the Early Termination Fee (and amount of financial security, as discussed in
Response to # 8) is being changed to equal the declining net book value of the assets, and such
net book value will always be lower than the Minimum Transmission Charge Liability Cap
(i.e., aggregate incremental revenue requirement for the Transmission Project over its useful
life), the substitute MTCA will be revised to indicate that the Early Termination Fee and
amount of financial security are not subject to the Minimum Transmission Charge Liability
Cap.

The substitute MTCA revises the Early Termination Fee in Section 14(F)(b) as follows:

       b. Early Termination Fee. If this MTCA is terminated and Customer is obligated to
          pay an Early Termination Fee, this will be calculated based on the month in which
          the effective date of termination occurs (the “Early Termination Fee”). The Early
 October 22, 2026
Page 8


           Termination Fee will equal the remaining net book value of the Transmission
           Project at the time of termination aggregate monthly Requested Transmission
           Capacity multiplied by the Network Rate in effect at the time of the termination
           event for the remainder of the Term of this MTCA. As referenced above in Section
           11 9, the Minimum Transmission Charge Liability Cap applies to any Early
           Termination Fee. The Early Termination Fee shall be updated upon termination, as
           described in this Section 14(F). Customer will pay the Early Termination Fee
           within seven days of receipt of an invoice following termination.



   7. Section 13 (Term) of the MTCA states that unless terminated earlier, the term of
      the MTCA shall commence on the effective date and continue until the later of 15
      years after the in-service date of the final tranche of transmission capacity, as
      defined by the requested transmission capacity schedule, or upon “payment of all
      outstanding payment obligations of [WEPCo] to ATC under this MTCA.”

               Please explain why 15 years after the in-service date of the final tranche of
               transmission capacity was selected as the term for the MTCA and why such
               a term for the MTCA is just and reasonable.

ATC Response:

The term of the MTCA was set at 15 years from the date the last of the transmission facilities
required to serve the load are placed in service to ensure that ATC’s other wholesale customers
do not incur costs related to WEPCo’s large load customer.

It is common that large loads ramp up over multiple years, with the various ramp increments
requiring additional transmission facilities. Thus, setting the 15-year term to start after all
required facilities are placed in service ensures that there is adequate time for WEPCo to pay
the resulting costs.

Also, the 15-year term was selected because it is consistent with the term set for WEPCo’s
Very Large Customer (VLC) Tariff approved by the PSCW. See PSCW Order at 15-16,
Docket 6630-TE-113 (May 21, 2026) (finding that a 15-year term of the VLC tariff “would
provide better protections to non-VLC customers and minimize the potential risks associated
with cost recovery, especially for transmission costs.”). Given that the Transmission Project
being constructed will have a useful life of approximately 30 years, ATC agrees with the
PSCW that 15-years will be sufficient time for WEPCo to make payments under the MTCA to
protect other wholesale customers from stranded costs. For these reasons, the proposed 15-year
term of the MTCA is just and reasonable.

    LARGE LOAD PROJECT COMMITMENT AGREEMENT (AREA 2A)
This LARGE LOAD PROJECT COMMITMENT AGREEMENT (AREA 2A) (“(“PCA” or “this
Agreement”) between, Wisconsin Electric Power Company, dba We Energies[LDC], a (“Local
Distribution Company” or “LDC”) and American Transmission Company LLC, a Wisconsin
limited liability company, by its corporate manager, ATC Management Inc., a Wisconsin
corporation (collectively, “ATC”) for a project known as Southeastern WI Economic
Development - Area 2A Load Interconnection and described in Exhibit A attached hereto
(“Project”) is executed on the latest date signed by the authorized representatives of each Party
and effective upon receipt of all required regulatory approvals contemplated by Section 3.11
hereof. ATC and the LDC each may be referred to as a “Party” or collectively as the “Parties.”
                                            RECITALS
WHEREAS, ATC is a public utility and transmission company under the laws of the State of
Wisconsin and owns, operates, and maintains an electric transmission system and provides
transmission service, including the interconnection of substations owned by others.
WHEREAS, ATC operates its transmission system under provisions of the Open Access
Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve Markets Tariff (“MISO Tariff”) of the Midcontinent
Independent Transmission System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”).
WHEREAS, LDC owns, operates, and maintains an electric distribution system that does or will
provide power to end-use customers in part via an interconnection to ATC’s transmission
system.
WHEREAS, ATC and LDC are parties to a Distribution-Transmission Interconnection
Agreement (“DTIA”), which has been filed at the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
(“FERC”).
WHEREAS, ATC and LDC are parties to a Minimum Transmission Charge Agreement
(“MTCA”), which is being executed in parallel with this PCA.
WHEREAS, LDC wishes to initiate a project that requires ATC’s completion of the Project,
including additions and/or modifications to ATC’s system or facilities (the “Affected Facilities”).


NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises and covenants contained herein,
and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby
acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
                                          AGREEMENT
                                            ARTICLE I
                             GENERAL PROVISIONS; PURPOSE
1.1 Incorporation of Recitals. The recitals set forth in the “Recitals” section are hereby
acknowledged by the Parties and incorporated into and made a part of this Agreement.
1.2 Collaboration. The Parties will collaborate in the design, construction and performance of
the services necessary for the construction of the Project.
1.3 Purpose. The purpose of this PCA is (a) to identify the initial conceptual design and
configuration of the Affected Facilities and designations of the common facilities; (b) to establish
a commitment by both Parties to make a good faith effort to meet the Project in-service date set
forth in Exhibit A hereto; (c) to set forth the obligation for both Parties to consult with each other
                                                                                PCA #: 2023-06

before terminating the Project; (d) to establish procedures for reimbursement of Project Costs
(defined below) in the case of Project cancellation or termination, or in the case of substantial
changes to the Project that might render existing work obsolete or unneeded; and (e) to
establish procedures for paying the return on Construction Work in Progress (“CWIP”) and
associated taxes related to the Project (“CWIP Charge”).
                                           ARTICLE II
                                   SCOPE AND SCHEDULE
2.1 Scope and Schedule. ATC shall commence and complete the work provided for under this
PCA according to the scope and schedule attached as Exhibit A to this PCA, and in accordance
with the DTIA.
2.2 Adjustments. The Parties shall jointly coordinate mutually agreeable scope and schedule
adjustments as necessary. After this PCA has been executed, any Party’s request to change
the in-service date of the Project and the other Party’s subsequent response must be made in
accordance with Article IV. This PCA may be amended and signed for changes to the in-
service date of 90 days or more or other changes. A revised PCA superseding and replacing
this PCA will be signed for any substantial changes in Project scope.
2.3 Reporting. ATC shall provide to LDC, on a monthly basis, the cumulative Project Costs
incurred on the Project to date as of the end of the prior month, as well as an estimate of the
Project Costs to be incurred or committed for the Project in the following three-month period.
ATC shall provide to LDC such additional reporting on the Project as the LDC reasonably
requests.
                                           ARTICLE III
                                  TERMS OF AGREEMENT
3.1 Role of DTIA. The work to be performed under this PCA will be performed in accordance
with the terms and conditions set forth in the DTIA between the Parties. To the extent that there
are conflicting terms or inconsistencies as between the DTIA and this PCA, this PCA shall
control.
3.2 Cancellation or Suspension; Effect. The Parties may, by written agreement, cancel or
suspend the Project. Either Party may unilaterally terminate the Project and this PCA upon
written notice to the other. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, if this PCA is jointly
terminated or if ATC unilaterally terminates this PCA, each Party shall be responsible for its own
incurred costs up to the date of cancellation or suspension without any invoicing of Project
Costs between the Parties. If LDC unilaterally terminates, cancels, or substantially changes the
Project such that work performed and/or materials and equipment procured by ATC is
unneeded or obsolete, or if the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin (“PSCW”) or Federal
Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC”) deny regulatory approvals necessary for completion
of the Project, LDC shall be obligated to reimburse the Project Costs as set forth below as well
as the CWIP Charge through the date of termination of this Agreement.
3.3 Obligation to Reimburse Project Costs. In consideration of the work performed by ATC,
LDC shall reimburse all expenditures, costs and cancellation fees incurred, or due to
commitments made, by ATC (collectively, “Project Costs”) as of the date of Project termination,
cancellation or substantial change. The reimbursement obligation set forth herein applies
immediately upon termination, cancellation or substantial change, and independent of any
payment due or made to LDC from its end-use customer under any separate agreement or
arrangement. In the event of termination of this PCA due to the completion of the Project, and
                                                                                 PCA #: 2023-06

the Project being put into ATC’s rate base (as described in Section 3.12(a)), the reimbursement
obligation set forth in this Section 3.3 shall not apply.
3.4 Amounts to be Reimbursed Upon Termination, Cancellation or Substantial Change. “Project
Costs” include (a) any purchase orders issued and/or contracts executed by ATC and accepted
by a third party for services, materials or equipment (including slot reservations); and (b) internal
costs of ATC, including fully loaded labor and expenses, related to the Project. Cost estimates
reflected in Exhibit A are estimated Project Costs only. Reimbursement shall be for actual
Project Costs, which shall include any applicable tax gross-up charges.
3.5 Amounts to Be Directly Charged. The CWIP Charge shall be directly charged monthly to,
and reimbursed by LDC, throughout the term of this Agreement, with such costs constituting the
carrying costs for the inclusion of CWIP associated with Project assets in ATC’s rate base
during the period of construction, commencing the month when CWIP is first recorded and
continuing through the month that the respective Project assets are placed in service. The
monthly CWIP Charge shall be based on the current month’s average CWIP balance and equal
the return on Project CWIP and shall include income taxes, as allowed in ATC’s formula rate on
Attachment O of the MISO Tariff. Estimated monthly CWIP Charges for the Project are set forth
on Exhibit C attached hereto. CWIP Charges reflected in Exhibit C are estimates only and shall
be calculated on a monthly basis, with charges based on actual CWIP-related expenses for a
given month, subject to an annual true up. Upon calculation of the annual true up, in the event
that LDC has underpaid CWIP Costs for the year, ATC shall issue an invoice for the deficit. In
the event that LDC has overpaid the annual CWIP costs, ATC shall issue a refund of such
overpaid amount within sixty (60) days of such calculation of the true up.
3.6 Mitigation. In the event LDC unilaterally terminates or cancels the Project with such
cancellation resulting in a reimbursement obligation to ATC for Project Costs incurred, ATC will
use reasonable efforts to mitigate those amounts to be reimbursed by LDC, including without
limitation repurposing or reselling equipment purchased for the Project if it can be repurposed or
resold (net of costs for the mitigation activities).
3.7 Payment of Reimbursable Project Costs. ATC shall issue an invoice to LDC reflecting
actual, reimbursable Project Costs incurred due to termination, cancellation or substantial
change, and LDC shall pay said invoice within sixty (60) days of issuance by ATC.
3.8 Payment of CWIP Charge. ATC shall issue an invoice to LDC reflecting actual CWIP
Charge incurred on a monthly basis, and LDC shall pay such invoices within thirty (30) days of
issuance by ATC. Any payments owed by LDC based upon the annual true up of CWIP Costs
shall be invoiced by ATC and paid by LDC within sixty (60) days of issuance by ATC.
3.9 Disputes. Any dispute that may arise between the Parties during the Project development
and interconnection process regarding schedule, scope, costs or any other matter, including a
request for reimbursement of costs by ATC resulting from LDC’s unilateral cancellation, delay of
more than ninety (90) days, or substantial changes to the Project, shall be subject to the Dispute
Resolution procedures of the DTIA.
3.10 Audit. ATC agrees that in the event LDC becomes obligated to pay Project Costs, LDC
shall have the right to audit such Project Costs, in accordance with the audit provisions set forth
in the DTIA.
3.11 Regulatory Filings. This Agreement is subject to FERC approval and may require
approval by the PSCW. As applicable, ATC shall file this Agreement with FERC, and ATC and
LDC shall jointly file an application for approval of this Agreement with the PSCW.
3.12 Termination. This Agreement shall terminate when: (a) ATC’s facilities required under this
Agreement are rolled into ATC’s transmission rates under the MISO Tariff, ATC is capable of
                                                                                 PCA #: 2023-06

providing electric service via the Project, and LDC has reimbursed all CWIP Charges related to
the Project; (b) the Project is terminated under Section 3.2 of this Agreement and ATC has
recovered reimbursement of the Project Costs and CWIP Charges from the LDC; (c) any
necessary regulatory approvals contemplated by Section 3.11 are denied; or (d) LDC terminates
the MTCA prior to the Project Assets going into service pursuant to Section 3.12(a) hereof.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, any termination under Section 3.12(c) or 3.12(d) shall not relieve
LDC from the reimbursement obligations set forth herein.

                                            NOTICES
All notices required hereunder shall be given in writing and addressed or delivered to the

validity of the remainder of this Agreement as long as the economic or legal substance of the

5.6 Headings and Captions. Article headings, section headings and/or other captions are
